your_book:
Jaleel's book had a good Monday session: by weight it was up roughly 0.7%, though unrealized performance is still slightly negative at -0.42%. The lift came from NVIDIA (+2.39% on a 7.4% weight), Abbott (+1.14% on 10.8%), Rocket Lab (+2.32%), On Holding (+2.03%) and Lululemon (+3.94%). Adobe (-1.97%) was the main drag, with Equifax (-2.08%) and Vertex (-1.23%) smaller. Zoetis, the largest weight at 11.5%, was flat at -0.07%.

Price and thesis are diverging in a few places. Rocket Lab (5.8% weight, -31.3% gain, AVOID, QARP 42.3) and Lululemon (4.0%, -19.5%, AVOID, QARP 52.0) both rallied, but together they are about 9.8% of the book in names the framework rates AVOID. Lululemon's flags (guidance cut, five straight quarters of Americas comp declines) haven't changed, so treat the bounce as a bounce. The tape also disagreed with the headlines. Chips were reported lower on AI-capex worries, yet NVIDIA and Broadcom both rose more than 2%. Software was reported higher, yet Adobe fell. Adobe's problem is narrative (AI-moat fear), not numbers, and today's move shows that.

Watch Boston Scientific (9.4%, -7.0%, STRONG BUY). Its guidance was cut and management guided flat through Q3, with earnings on Oct 28, two sessions out. The score and the price are pulling apart ahead of that print.

attention.headline: Earnings Oct 28 on a 9.4% weight
attention.note: Guidance was cut to 7–8.5% growth with management guiding flat through Q3, the position is down 7.0%, and the print lands two sessions after Tuesday's, so the sizing decision comes before the event.

attention.headline: AVOID-rated, -31.3%, and bounced
attention.note: A 5.8% weight in a name scored AVOID (QARP 42.3) rose 2.32% today, so check whether the position is still justified rather than letting the bounce settle it.

attention.headline: +3.94% rally against an unchanged thesis
attention.note: The guidance cut, tariff margin damage and stalled China are still in place, the next catalyst is Dec 9, and the position is still -19.5% at AVOID.

attention.headline: Fell 1.97% while software rose
attention.note: The sell-off is driven by AI-disruption fear rather than results, and it widened on a day when the sector headline was positive.
